data.title: Implementation reliability: reduce bugs, test failures, and review findings via better initial code

content.text: **Problem.** Implementation sub-agents and the implementation-plan skill currently produce code that requires multiple review/test cycles to land. A meaningful share of bugs, test failures, and code-review findings could be eliminated if initial code quality were higher — driven by better context (what to read first, what conventions to follow, which prior art exists) and better prompting (what the agent should explicitly check before declaring done).

**Goal.** Calibrate the context provided to and prompting of implementation sub-agents and /dso:implementation-plan so that the rate of post-implementation review findings, test failures, and follow-up bug tickets per merge drops — without lengthening the overall implementation cycle.

**Approach (to be brainstormed).** Coordinates with several existing tactical epics (2ca5-26ef sprint reference injection, f7d5-59e4 impl-plan citation, 9ddd-117b architect pattern, ab57-b534 experimental verification, 6111-fc7f execution trace, dso-r97p impl-plan schema validation) but is distinct: it owns the calibration loop — measuring initial-code defect rate and driving context/prompting changes to reduce it.
**Out of scope.** New stacks/runners; architecture changes to the implementation-plan pipeline itself.
Created as a North Star placeholder during /dso:prioritize-epics Phase 2; refine via /dso:brainstorm.
